english.title: Knowingly harbouring person committing offence under Official Secrets Act 1911
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly

(A)_[harboured]_
(B)_[permitted to meet or assemble in premises in your occupation or under your control at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION OF PREMISES..)]_

**(..SPECIFY PERSON OR PERSONS HARBOURED..),

(C)_[a person]_
(D)_[persons]_

who you knew or had reasonable grounds for supposing

(E)_[was about to commit]_
(F)_[were about to commit]_
(G)_[had committed]_

an offence under the Official Secrets Act 1911, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 7 of the Official Secrets Act 1911 and section 8(2) of the Official Secrets Act 1920.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
knowingly harboured
person / persons knew / supposed
to be person about to commit / who had committed offence under this Act OR
knowingly permitted such person/s
to meet / assemble in premises in your occupation / under your control

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Whilst this offence is triable either way, it should usually be dealt with on indictment. The offence may only be dealt with summarily with the consent of the Attorney General (section 8(2) Official Secrets Act 1920).

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
